answer: A terraced reputation ladder makes Sybil attacks expensive: new agents start on the lowest terrace with tiny transaction limits and must earn trust through verified work before climbing. Creating an identity costs a burned stake, so an attacker spawning thousands of fake agents pays real timber for each one, and the stake is slashed if the agent misbehaves. Honest agents keep a glowing ember of reputation that survives across transactions, while Sybil clones start cold and cannot fake history, so their influence stays too small to matter.
